lead_with.title: Transformation needs a location answer
lead_with.text: Standard Chartered is in the **final year of its Fit for Growth programme** (2026) and, at its **May 2026 investor event**, targeted a **cost-to-income ratio of about 57% by 2028** (63% in 2025) and **about 20% more income per employee**. Ask Timothy how transformation decisions about **where work is done** are made, and by whom.

lead_with.title: New York hours at about half the cost
lead_with.text: SC runs its Americas business from **New York**. A Finance Montréal-commissioned 2026 cost study puts a 150-person financial operation at about **US$18.9M/yr in Montreal vs US$35.3M in New York**, in the **same time zone**. Relevant for Americas-hours cash, payments, client-service or controls support.

lead_with.title: A Canada foothold without a branch
lead_with.text: SC has **no current Canadian operation** found. An IFC-eligible support team in Montreal could serve the **Americas franchise** with the **Quebec IFC tax credit (24% of eligible salaries, up to C$18,000 per employee per year, min. 6 eligible staff)**, in a **bilingual** city where BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, State Street and Morgan Stanley already operate.

person.name: Timothy Tan
person.text: **Associate Director, Cash Service Strategy & Transformation** at Standard Chartered in **Singapore** (per his LinkedIn headline and Streak). Prior roles, education and time at the bank are **to be confirmed** on his LinkedIn profile: no press coverage of him was found. He is **mid-level**, so treat him as a friendly **door-opener and internal champion** to the operations and transformation leaders who decide on locations. In the LinkedIn exchange he was **warm and quick**: 'happy to meet up', and gave a **personal Gmail** rather than a bank address (keep early messages light and non-confidential).

company.text: Standard Chartered is a UK-headquartered international bank (founded 1853) with most of its income from **Asia, Africa and the Middle East**. Its **Transaction Services** business (payments and liquidity, trade, securities services) earned **$6.0B in 2025 (-7%)**; **Payments & Liquidity**, which includes cash management, earned **$4.2B (-10%)** on lower interest rates despite strong balance growth. **Wealth Solutions** grew **24%** to **$3.1B**. At its **May 2026 investor event** the bank set targets of **RoTE above 15% in 2028 and about 18% in 2030**, 5-7% income CAGR to 2028, and a **reduction of more than 15% of corporate-function roles by 2030**, while scaling automation and AI. It already runs **Global Business Services** hubs, including in **India, Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur) and Warsaw** (Warsaw opened 2018 as the GBS hub outside Asia). In the Americas, SC has its **regional HQ in New York** plus offices in Argentina, Brazil and Colombia; **no Canadian office** is listed.

financials.text: **FY2025:** underlying operating income **$20.9B** (+6%; +8% ex notable items), underlying profit before tax **$7.9B** (+18% at constant currency), reported PBT **$7.0B**, underlying RoTE **14.7%** (13% target hit a year early), underlying EPS **229.7 cents** (+37%), CET1 **14.1%**; Transaction Services **$6.0B** (-7%); new **$1.5B** buyback. Source: SC full-year 2025 results, Feb 24, 2026. **H1 2026:** record operating income **$11.6B** (+6%), profit before tax **$4.8B** (+9%), RoTE **17.6%**, EPS **151.6 cents** (+17%), operating expenses **$6.3B** (+1%); Wealth Solutions +38%, Global Banking +19%. 2026 guidance raised to income growth around the middle of 5-7% and costs of about **$13.3B**. Source: SC half-year 2026 results, Jul 29, 2026. Headcount not checked here (to be confirmed).

industry.title: Banks are cutting cost-to-income through location and automation
industry.text: SC's own plan (57% cost-to-income by 2028, >15% fewer corporate-function roles by 2030, more AI) is typical: banks are re-deciding which work sits in high-cost centres like New York.

industry.title: Cash management under margin pressure
industry.text: Falling interest rates cut SC's Payments & Liquidity income 10% in 2025 even as balances grew, which pushes cash businesses to **lower their cost to serve** and transform operations.

industry.title: IFC tax credit
industry.text: Quebec's International Financial Centre measure gives **24% of eligible salaries, up to C$18,000 per employee per year** (min. 6 eligible staff) for qualifying international financial activities and support. Whether specific cash-services roles qualify is **to be confirmed** case by case.

industry.title: Montreal's financial depth
industry.text: Bilingual workforce, **New York time zone**, and a base of international banks already present: **BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, State Street, Morgan Stanley**.

talking_points: What does **Cash Service Strategy & Transformation** cover: client-facing cash management products, or the operating model behind them?
Where do SC's **Americas cash and payments operations** sit today (New York, GBS hubs in India/Malaysia/Warsaw)? Is there a need for **Americas-hours** coverage closer to clients?
How does the bank decide **new locations** for operations and transformation programmes, and who owns those decisions?
Would a one-page **Montreal vs New York cost and IFC-credit comparison** for a small Americas support team help him make the case internally?
Could he **introduce Noza** to the operations, GBS or Americas COO-level person who looks at location strategy?
